wages.text: She supports raising the minimum wage and protecting gig workers and union organizing.
wages.quote: Raising the minimum wage and protecting gig workers and union organizing efforts.

immigration.text: She supports ending harmful ICE enforcement and creating faster, lower-cost citizenship pathways.
immigration.quote: I support ending harmful enforcement systems like ICE and creating safer, faster pathways to citizenship that do not depend on high costs or long delays.

abortion.text: She says she would protect reproductive freedom and the right to choose.
abortion.quote: Protect reproductive freedom and the right to choose.

gender.text: Her campaign supports nationwide protections for transgender and non-binary people, including against discriminatory bathroom bills.
gender.quote: Nationwide protections for transgender and non-binary individuals, including the right to accurate gender markers on IDs and protections from discriminatory “bathroom bills.”

health.text: She supports Medicare for All and universal, affordable, and accessible healthcare.
health.quote: Expanding affordable housing programs and supporting Medicare for All to ease financial burdens.

voting.text: She supports expanding early and mail voting, automatic registration, and federal anti-suppression protections.
voting.quote: I support expanding early voting, mail voting, and automatic registration, and creating strong federal protections against voter suppression.

tax.text: He supported tax cuts in the Working Families Tax Cuts legislation and said families can spend their money better than Washington bureaucrats.
tax.quote: I believe Kentucky families know how to better spend their money than bureaucrats in Washington. I am proud of the work our Republican majority accomplished to secure these tax cuts.

wages.text: He voted against the Raise the Wage Act, which would have increased the federal minimum wage.

debt.text: He said reforms should protect Social Security and Medicare for current seniors and keep the programs available for future generations.
debt.quote: I support reforms that protect Social Security and Medicare for today’s seniors, and that will ensure they exist for future generations.

housing.text: He requested funding for a planned workforce-housing community of 1,100 to 1,500 units.
housing.quote: This funding will be used for land acquisition of a critical parcel of land adjacent to the Kentucky Transpark, for a planned housing community that will include 1,100–1,500 units, co-located amenities, and the new Oakland Elementary School.

schools.text: He co-hosted a House Republican roundtable described as work for school choice and parental rights.
schools.quote: Representatives James Comer, Brett Guthrie, Jim Banks, Victoria Spartz, hosted a roundtable to highlight how one-party rule has failed our children and how House Republicans are working for school choice and parental rights.

safety.text: He requested federal funding for a sheriff’s department tactical team for high-risk response efforts.
safety.quote: The funding would be used by a full-service law enforcement agency with 78 personnel to help assemble a tactical team to assist in barricade hostage resolution and high-risk response efforts.

immigration.text: He said border security should come first and opposed amnesty while identifying agriculture and high-tech research as areas for immigration reform.
immigration.quote: First, we must secure the border. Beyond that, the most critical areas of reform are in agriculture and high-tech research. I do not support amnesty.

guns.text: He said the Second Amendment protects an individual right to bear arms and that he does not favor additional gun control.
guns.quote: I believe the 2nd Amendment protects an individual’s right to keep and bear arms. I don’t favor additional gun control.

abortion.text: He described himself as pro-life and cited his endorsement from the Kentucky Right to Life PAC.
abortion.quote: I am pro-life, and am proud to be endorsed by the Kentucky Right to Life PAC.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

cannabis.text: He said he opposed legalizing marijuana, while distinguishing industrial hemp from marijuana legalization.
cannabis.quote: I oppose legalizing marijuana. I did vote for legalizing industrial hemp as part of the Farm Bill that passed this year.

health.text: He favored market-based health care approaches that he said would lower costs and keep decisions between patients and doctors.
health.quote: I do think there are better market-based approaches that would actually lower costs and keep decisions between patients and doctors.

energy.text: He supported an energy strategy including Kentucky coal and said domestic energy production should be encouraged.
energy.quote: I support an all-of-the-above strategy that includes Kentucky coal. We need to encourage domestic energy production, not stifle it.

voting.text: He promoted the SAVE America Act's photo-ID, proof-of-citizenship, and voter-roll provisions.
voting.quote: This bill will mandate the use of photo ID to vote, require proof of citizenship to register to vote, and establish programs to support the removal of existing non-citizens from state voter rolls.
